Resolves #19755

The Playwright 1.64 / cssnano 9.6 update now preserves Playwright's disabled features and keeps flex-sized grids within their allocated viewport. Chromium 156 exposes Grid's automatic minimum height with the existing `hidden/clip` overflow pair; a grid-only `min-height: 0` restores the original layout. Real drag and divider assertions are retained, with bounds checks so off-screen gestures and out-of-image samples fail directly. Numeric Flexbox semantics stay unchanged.

Change class: restoration.
Evidence: L3 (real pointer and screenshot controls in the component composition) → L3 required (AC-2/3). No installed Fleet claim.
agent-preflight: not hosted here; local commit guards and hosted baseline checks passed.

## Deltas from ticket

Isolation found a Grid minimum-size issue, rather than an input-dispatch or cssnano failure. The ticket body now records that cause and the owning SCSS repair. Existing component witnesses gained bounds guards; no gesture, timeout or product expectation was relaxed.

## Test Evidence

Node 24.19; cssnano held at 9.3.2 for the controls; the component fixture uses development CSS (the theme builder invokes cssnano only for esm/production).

Final `09c1236` was also installed from its exact lockfile under Node 24.19 (Playwright 1.64 / cssnano 9.6, no comparison links): all 15 owning component cases pass in 13.0s. The final Grid CSS also passes the three original diagnostic assertions on Chromium 153 in 6.5s, with no CSS overlay.

| Runner / browser / Grid CSS | Result |
|---|---|
| Playwright 1.63 / Chromium 153 / unchanged | All 15 cases in the three full component files pass. |
| Playwright 1.64 / Chromium 156 / unchanged | The same 3 failures as hosted CI; 12 pass. |
| Playwright 1.64 / Chromium 153 / unchanged | All 3 targeted diagnostic cases pass. |
| Playwright 1.64 / Chromium 156 / only Grid `min-height:0` overlaid | All 3 original diagnostic assertions pass. |

With Chromium 156, the 720px Viewport contained Grid heights 273px + 720px; the ordinary drag pressed at y807 and targeted HTML. Eight divider samples were below the 900px PNG and returned transparent zero bytes. Chromium 153 computed Grid overflow as hidden/hidden; 156 computed hidden/clip. Explicit Grid minimum height zero retains hidden/clip and `flex:1 1 0%` while restoring 360px + 360px allocation, real scrolling and in-bounds divider samples.

Reproduce the full component selection with the explicit config:
```sh
npm run test-components -- test/playwright/component/grid/ClickFocus.spec.mjs test/playwright/component/grid/DragScrollNativeDrag.spec.mjs test/playwright/component/grid/ColumnTrailingEdge.spec.mjs --workers=1
```

### 🔬 Depth Floor

- **Challenge**: In `resources/scss/src/grid/Container.scss:17-20`, `.neo-grid-container` pairs `overflow-x: hidden` with `overflow-y: clip` and now explicitly sets `min-height: 0` because `overflow-y: clip` is not a scroll container on the Y axis in Chromium 156 (so automatic minimum size on the Y axis defaults to `auto` rather than `0`). On the horizontal axis, `overflow-x: hidden` still qualifies as a scroll container so `min-width` resolves to `0` automatically; however, if `.neo-grid-container` is ever placed inside a `flex-direction: row` parent and `overflow-x` is later changed from `hidden` to `clip`, `min-width: 0` would be needed symmetrically. Non-blocking for this PR since `overflow-x: hidden` remains in place.

### 🧠 Graph Ingestion Notes

*   **`[RETROSPECTIVE]`**: In Chromium 156, `overflow-x: hidden; overflow-y: clip` computes as `hidden/clip` rather than coercing `clip` to `hidden`; because `overflow-y: clip` is not a scroll container, flex items with `overflow-y: clip` require explicit `min-height: 0` (`resources/scss/src/grid/Container.scss`) to shrink within their flex allocation. Additionally, Canvas `getImageData(x, y, 1, 1)` returns transparent black (`0,0,0,0`) for out-of-bounds coordinates without throwing, so screenshot pixel witnesses (`ColumnTrailingEdge.spec.mjs`) must guard `0 <= x < image.width` and `0 <= y < image.height` explicitly.
